title: Open the gates at the Kennel
text: The locals want an open session at the Kennel on Sunday, kids on shoulders along the fence. The coaches would rather work without a crowd.

choices.label: Open the gates
choices.result: The fence is three deep. The players feel the suburb behind them, and the session never quite settles.

choices.label: Train behind closed doors
choices.result: A clean week of work. The locals feel shut out, and the board hears about it.

title: The men's health night in the west
text: The club's men's health night is on at a community hall out west on Tuesday, and the organisers want {name} to front a session. It's a recovery week.

choices.label: Send {first}

effects.why: The club turned up for the blokes of the west

choices.result: {name} has the hall laughing and talking. It's a late one in a recovery week.

choices.label: Send someone from the staff
choices.result: {name} keeps his routine. The organisers are polite about it, but they wanted a player.

title: Who pays for the women's health program?
text: The club's community arm wants to start a women's health program across the west, and it's short of money. The board asks whether the football department will give up part of its budget.

choices.label: Fund it from the football budget

effects.why: The club looked after the families of the west

choices.result: The program starts on time. The football department runs a few fewer sessions this month.

choices.label: Leave it to the community arm to find sponsors

effects.hit_result: A local business steps in and the program starts on time.
effects.miss_result: No sponsor comes, the program waits a year, and the west notices.

choices.result: The football budget stays whole while the community arm knocks on doors.

title: The word "merger" is in the paper
text: The club is in debt, and the paper says league headquarters is sounding out a merger partner for the Dogs. The supporters are already talking about a rally at the Kennel.

choices.label: Back the supporters' rally in public

hit.why: The supporters raised the money to save their club

effects.hit_result: The tins come back full. The debt falls and the Kennel has never been louder.
effects.miss_result: The rally falls short, and the board wears a public fight with the league.

choices.result: The coach stands with the supporters, and the whole league hears it.

choices.label: Say nothing and let the board negotiate

effects.why: The supporters felt their coach left them on their own

choices.result: The board keeps control of the talks. The supporters and the players are left wondering.

title: The stickers are back on the cars
text: The league has done the Dogs no favours again, and supporters have printed stickers telling headquarters what they think. A reporter asks you whether you've got one.

choices.label: "I've got two."

effects.why: The coach stood with the supporters against the league

choices.result: The supporters love it and the rooms have a laugh. League headquarters is not amused, and the board hears about it.

choices.label: "We just play the fixture we're given."

effects.why: The supporters think the coach has gone soft on the league

choices.result: The board is relieved. Out in Footscray, they reckon the coach has gone soft.

title: A regional city wants home games
text: A big regional city to the west has offered the club a paid deal to play home games at its ground each season. Footscray is split.

choices.label: Take two games a year

effects.hit_result: The bus trip home takes it out of them.

choices.result: Steady money and a new heartland. Two home crowds go up the highway.

choices.label: Take one game

effects.hit_result: The trip still costs them some legs.

choices.result: Some money and some goodwill. The city wanted two.

choices.label: Keep every home game in Melbourne

effects.why: The members kept every home game

choices.result: The members keep their games. The board loses money it had budgeted for.

title: Sell a home game to the Top End?
text: A government up north has offered strong money for a Dogs home game in the dry heat. The players lose a week of routine and the members lose a home game.

choices.label: Sell it

effects.why: The members gave up a home game for the money

choices.result: A big cheque comes in. The heat and the flights take something out of the side, and the members grumble.

choices.label: Keep it at home

effects.why: The members kept their game at home

choices.result: The members are pleased and the side keeps its routine. The board misses the money.

title: A kid from the western suburbs wants a go
text: A raw teenager from a local junior club, son of migrants, has been tearing up the local league. The recruiters say he's two years away, maybe more.

choices.label: Give him a spot on the list

hit.why: A kid from the west grew into a senior footballer

effects.hit_result: He keeps growing, and the west watches every step.
effects.miss_result: He doesn't come on, and the spot was a ready-made player's.

choices.result: The west hears the Dogs have backed one of their own.

choices.label: Let him train with the reserves

effects.hit_result: Another club lists him before the Dogs make up their mind.

choices.result: No list spot used, and the club keeps an eye on him.

choices.label: Pass on him
choices.result: The list stays as planned. The local juniors hear the club passed on one of their own.

title: The Footscray market wants the Dogs
text: The traders at the market want players there on Saturday morning, every stall in red, white and blue. It's the morning after a road trip.

choices.label: Send a group of players

effects.why: The players turned up for their own suburb

effects.hit_result: Tired legs from the trip catch up with them.

choices.result: The market is packed and the stallholders are thrilled.

choices.label: Send the mascot and the cheer squad
choices.result: The players rest. The traders wanted players, and the market talks.

title: The old bloke in the outer
text: At the members' function, an old supporter tells you he's waited most of his life for a flag and hasn't got many seasons left. A reporter overhears.

choices.label: "We'll do it for him."
choices.result: It's in the paper by morning. The members and the players are fired up, and every loss now carries a promise.

choices.label: "Every supporter's waited. We'll keep working."

effects.why: The coach kept the talk on the work

choices.result: No promise to answer for. Some of the members wanted more fire.

title: Nobody's tipping us
text: The Dogs have made the finals from low on the ladder, and every pundit has them out next week. The players want to know how the coach will play it.

choices.label: "Let them write us off."
choices.result: The rooms go in with a chip on the shoulder. Some of the younger ones are wound tight.

choices.label: "We respect them, and we back ourselves."
choices.result: No extra noise. The players wanted the coach to back them louder.

title: The membership drive in the west
text: The Dogs have always had fewer members than the big Melbourne clubs. Marketing wants the coach and the players on a membership tour of the western suburbs.

choices.label: Players at every event
choices.result: Membership grows. The players are busy, and it shows early in the season.

choices.label: The coach goes, the players stay home
choices.result: Some new members sign up. The coach misses a few sessions on the road, and marketing wanted players.

choices.label: No tour, focus on the football
choices.result: A clean pre-season. Membership stays flat, and the board is disappointed.

title: The club wants out of gambling money
text: A big share of the club's income comes from gambling in its own suburb. The president wants out because it takes money from the very people the club is for; the finance staff warn about the hole it leaves.

choices.label: Back the exit in public

effects.why: The members respect the club walking away from gambling money
The club chose its suburb over easy money

choices.result: The community and the members respect it. The money it leaves behind will take years to replace.

choices.label: Keep the income and say nothing

effects.why: The club kept taking gambling money from its own suburb

choices.result: The money keeps coming. Community groups criticise the club, and the president is annoyed.

title: The members want the old guernsey back
text: A members' group is pushing for the club to wear its old guernsey for one home game a year. Marketing says the current one is what sells.

choices.label: Back the members

effects.why: The coach stood with the old faithful

choices.result: The old faithful are delighted. Marketing is put out.

choices.label: "That's above my pay grade."

effects.why: The members expected the coach to stand with them

choices.result: No fight with the board. Some members expected the coach to stand with them.

title: A new bulldog for the boundary
text: The club's bulldog mascot is retiring to a quiet backyard. The cheer squad wants the players to pick his replacement from three pups at the Kennel.

choices.label: Make a day of it, players and pups
choices.result: A lovely morning for the rooms and the fans. Half a session goes to the pups.

choices.label: Let the cheer squad choose
choices.result: No time lost. The fans wanted the players involved.

title: One of the greats is at training
text: One of the club's greats, a name on the honour boards at the Kennel, has turned up and asked to say a few words to the players. He's old school and doesn't do soft.

choices.label: Hand him the huddle

effects.why: A club great told the players what the jumper means

effects.hit_result: Some of it lands badly with the younger ones.

choices.result: The young ones will remember it.

choices.label: Thank him, and save him for the members' lunch
choices.result: The week runs to plan. He's a bit hurt, and it gets around.

title: Build it or buy it?
text: A proven star at another club wants to come to the Dogs, but the price is the club's first-round pick. The recruiters have always prided themselves on growing their own.

choices.label: Pay the price for the star

effects.why: The club went after a proven star

effects.hit_result: He never quite settles, and the rooms feel it.

choices.result: An instant best-22 player. The first-round pick is gone.

choices.label: Keep the pick and back the draft

effects.why: The club backed its recruiters to grow their own

choices.result: The recruiters get their pick. The star goes to a rival, and the board wanted the ambition.

title: The hard runner in the twos
text: {name} has been killing it in the reserves, and the critics say he isn't up to the big league. The Dogs have a long line of blokes who proved the critics wrong.

choices.label: Pick him to tag their best midfielder

hit.why: You gave him a job and he did it

effects.hit_result: He holds his man, and the job is his.
effects.miss_result: He gets beaten and goes back to the twos.

choices.result: {name} gets his chance with the hardest job on the ground.

choices.label: Keep him in the twos another month

effects.why: He wonders when his chance comes

choices.result: {name} keeps building. He wonders when his chance comes.

title: The cheer squad's banner
text: The cheer squad paints its banner in a shed near the Kennel the night before every game. This week they've asked if a few players could help with the last letters.

choices.label: Send the leadership group

effects.why: The leaders painted the banner with the cheer squad

choices.result: The squad is over the moon. The leaders get home late.

choices.label: Send a signed ball and a thank-you

effects.why: The cheer squad wanted players, not a signed ball

choices.result: No disruption to the week. The squad wanted players.

title: Two seniors short of a gallop
text: Two senior players are back from injury but short of touch. The development coach wants both sent to the reserves this week for a full game.

choices.label: Send both down
choices.result: Both get a full game in the twos. Neither is pleased to be dropped, and the group notices.

choices.label: Send one, keep one
choices.result: One gets his game in the twos. The other is still short of a gallop.

title: Who owns the west?
text: {opp} have billboards up all over the western suburbs this week, right in the Dogs' backyard. The players have noticed.

choices.label: "The west is ours."
choices.result: The group is fired up. Lose this one and the gloating will be everywhere.

choices.label: Keep it about the football

effects.why: The coach kept the week on the football
The supporters wanted the coach to make a statement

choices.result: No extra pressure. The supporters wanted a statement.

title: The local business or the big one
text: A family business in Footscray has sponsored the club through the thin times. A big national company has offered more for the same spot, and the board wants the coach's view.

choices.label: Stay loyal to the local

effects.why: The club stuck by a family that stuck by it

choices.result: The community and the members love it. The club leaves money on the table.

choices.label: Take the big money

effects.why: Footscray heard the club dropped a local family for money

choices.result: More money for the club. The local family is hurt, and Footscray hears about it.

title: A late night ends in the paper
text: Two Dogs players were in a fight outside a city nightclub after a win. Nobody was badly hurt, but it's on the front page.

choices.label: Suspend both for a week

effects.why: The club made its standards clear

choices.result: The standards are clear. Two players sit out, and the group is split on it.

choices.label: Fine them and handle it in-house
choices.result: Both play. The press say the club has gone soft, and the board agrees.

title: A positive test leaks
text: A Dogs player has returned a positive test for an illicit drug, and it has leaked before the club can speak. His family is asking the club to protect him.

choices.label: Stand by him and get him help

effects.why: The club looked after one of its own

choices.result: The playing group appreciates the loyalty. The press and parts of the board call it soft.

choices.label: Stand him down until it's dealt with

effects.why: The club held the line on drugs

choices.result: The board is satisfied. The group thinks the club dropped one of its own.

title: The board meets after a fifth loss
text: Five straight losses, and the president has called a board meeting. The old players on the board want to know whether the coach has a plan or an excuse.

choices.label: Blood the kids now
choices.result: The board gives the coach time. The young ones get games, and the results may get worse first.

choices.label: Promise to win now with the experienced players

effects.hit_result: The next fortnight goes badly, and the board remembers the promise.

choices.result: The senior players feel backed. The board will judge the coach on results.

title: The juniors want the Kennel
text: The western suburbs junior league wants its grand finals at the Kennel on the club's main training day. The seniors would have to use the back field.

choices.label: Give them the ground

effects.why: The west's footy families feel the Kennel is theirs too

choices.result: The junior clubs have the day of their lives. The seniors make do on the back field.

choices.label: Keep the main ground for the seniors
choices.result: Preparation is untouched. The junior clubs feel second best, and it gets around.
